title: Sunny and the Bush Silence
description: Little Sonny the quokka learns to sit with the deep, beautiful silence of the bush. A slow, peaceful bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
One afternoon, Sunny went looking for something.

He wasn't sure what. He just felt like there was something he needed, and he didn't know quite what it was.

He walked for a while through the bush. He listened. He looked.

And then he came to a small clearing he had never found before. Just a round, open patch of ground, ringed by tall gum trees. A small grey rock sat in the middle. Grass grew in sparse tufts around it.

Sunny sat on the rock.

And then he noticed it.

The silence.

Not a full silence — there was still the wind, and a distant bird, and the quiet hum of the world going on. But underneath all of that, something deep and still. A quiet that went down and down, below all the sounds.

Sunny sat very, very still and tried to feel it.

He breathed in slowly. He breathed out.

He didn't think about yesterday or tomorrow. He just felt the rock beneath him and the air around him and the big, easy presence of the bush.

Somewhere above him, a leaf let go of a branch and floated down in a slow spiral.

Sunny watched it all the way to the ground.

The silence held him. It didn't feel like nothing. It felt like everything, soft and still.

He understood, now, what he had been looking for.

This. Just this.

He sat a while longer, until the golden evening light touched the tops of the gum trees.

Then he walked home slowly, carrying the silence with him like something precious.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, quiet clearing. Goodnight, deep and beautiful silence.
